title: Fix inverted on/off semantics of toggle bar
head: 3110117e52cc
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Two open presentation-mode PRs become backwards with this bar API
leads.consequence: Both divergent, currently open PRs explicitly promise to hide the bar on presentation on and restore its prior visible state on off. Each calls omarchy-toggle-bar on during enable and off during restore, exactly opposite this PR's changed wrapper. After either presentation PR lands alongside this fix, presentation on leaves a previously visible bar visible (or reveals a previously hidden bar), and off hides a formerly visible bar (or fails to re-hide one originally hidden). Their first bar visibility assertion fails. Neither command returns an error, and a later presentation on still fails to hide it. Update the presentation callers and tests (on -> off; off -> on) in whichever PR lands, or coordinate merging before this semantics change.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator from #12422/#12730 diffs (omarchy-toggle-presentation calls `on` to hide, `off` to restore; no file overlap); Opus R2/R3 confirmed test failure on combined tree; published

leads.summary: Open help-only PR #11803 cleanly combines with this fix but documents the reverse behaviour
leads.location: bin/omarchy-toggle-bar:3-5; #11803's addition to summary at line 3
leads.consequence: Patch of divergent open #11803 onto this head applies without conflict, leaving the help summary '(on hides the bar, off shows it)' while the new case maps on to removing bar-off and off to creating it. The CLI help and commands metadata (and users following them) will give exactly wrong instructions; first subsequent call on shows the bar. Coordinate withdrawing or revising #11803's summary before both merge.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator from #11803 diff and bin/omarchy summary parsing; published

leads.summary: Changed shell test no longer constructs the half-hidden state it claims to exercise
leads.consequence: After line 71 clears both flags, line 75 now calls bar on, which clears an already absent bar-off flag. Thus line 76 starts with both flags absent, not one half enabled. A plausible broken fullscreen implementation that toggles the two flags independently instead of reconciling asymmetric states passes every kept assertion (13 successes in the isolated run), while entering fullscreen from hidden-bar/normal-gaps would instead show the bar. Set bar off at line 75, assert bar-off present and window-no-gaps absent before toggling, and check both flags remain present afterward; also directly check no-arg bar toggle used by menu/hotkey.

leads.summary: Malformed bar arguments still report success after the underlying toggle rejects them
leads.consequence: For an unrecognized action such as bogus, the default arm forwards it to omarchy-toggle, which writes a usage error and exits 1 without changing bar-off. The wrapper has no set -e or exit status propagation and continues to its final omarchy-shell -q command, which returns 0 even if the shell is unavailable; callers see success for a no-op. The previous simple wrapper also had this defect, so this is an inherited argument edge case in the rewritten dispatch, not an introduced on/off regression. A subsequent valid call works. Reject invalid actions in this case, or propagate the helper failure before the IPC nudge.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (pre-existing exit 0 on unknown args); corroboration; published as Optional

leads.summary: Four other open fixes edit these same toggle files and need explicit resolution
leads.consequence: Open #12150, #12155 and #13451 each modify all four of this PR's files to implement substantially the same on/off inversion, and open #7023 modifies the bar script and two tests without the fullscreen adjustment. The PR heads are divergent, not stacked. Applying their focused diffs to this PR head rejects the bar-script hunks (and for the three four-file PRs also the fullscreen hunks); do not treat GitHub's individual MERGEABLE-vs-current-base result as mergeable against this head. Maintain one canonical fix and consciously resolve the tests if another is selected, instead of blindly combining incompatible hunks. This is a merge/coordination hazard, not evidence that both normalized implementations would misbehave once resolved.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the fix gives `omarchy toggle bar on/off` the documented meaning. The no-argument form used by the hotkey and menu still flips the bar, and the full-screen desktop toggle ends in the same state as before. One shell test case no longer sets up the state it names, and three related open PRs would conflict with the new semantics if merged alongside it.

| Command (isolated run, `bar-off` flag result) | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `omarchy-toggle-bar on` | flag set (bar hidden) | flag cleared (bar shown) |
| `omarchy-toggle-bar off` | flag cleared (bar shown) | flag set (bar hidden) |
| no argument, `""`, `toggle` | flips | flips |
| `omarchy toggle bar on/off` via the `omarchy` dispatcher | inverted | on shows, off hides |
| `omarchy-toggle-fullscreen-desktop` (4 start states × 6 argument forms) | reference | identical final flags and exit status in all 24 cases |

**Verified (callers):** the `SUPER + SHIFT + SPACE` binding (`default/hypr/bindings/utilities.lua:16`) and the menu entry (`default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc:95`) call `omarchy-toggle-bar` with no argument, so they are unaffected. `Bar.qml` reads the flag file (and the notifications service reads the bar's hidden state), and the flag's meaning (present = hidden) is unchanged, so existing installs keep their current bar state and no migration is needed. Apart from the full-screen toggle and the tests this PR updates, no script, migration or doc in the repository passes `on`/`off` to the bar toggle.

**Verified (tests):** the updated `test/shell.d/toggle-test.sh` passes on the PR head and fails on the base scripts at `bar off sets the bar-off flag to hide the bar`. The swapped acceptance test (`session-test.sh`) is consistent with the new meaning; it was read, not run.

### Full-screen "half-hidden" test case no longer starts half-hidden

`test/shell.d/toggle-test.sh:75` still calls `omarchy-toggle-bar on`. Before this PR that set `bar-off`, giving a bar-hidden, gaps-on desktop. Now it clears a flag that line 71 already cleared, so the case at lines 76-77 starts from a fully visible desktop and repeats the earlier "enter full screen" case.

```text
state just before line 76      bar-off   window-no-gaps
base scripts + base test       set       absent          (half-hidden, as named)
PR scripts   + PR test         absent    absent          (fully visible)
```

**Impact:** the pull-into-line rule at `bin/omarchy-toggle-fullscreen-desktop:13` is no longer tested. Two diagnostic mutants of that rule (decide by `bar-off` alone; `||` instead of `&&`) pass the PR's test but are caught by the base test and by the corrected line below.

**Suggested change:**

```diff
-HOME="$test_home" omarchy-toggle-bar on
+HOME="$test_home" omarchy-toggle-bar off
```

With this change the PR scripts still pass and both mutants fail at `fullscreen toggle pulls a half-hidden desktop into full screen`.

### Related open PRs rely on the old meaning

These PRs apply cleanly to the current base but assume the pre-fix behaviour:

- **#12422** and **#12730** add `bin/omarchy-toggle-presentation`, which calls `omarchy-toggle-bar on` to hide the bar when presentation mode starts and `omarchy-toggle-bar off` to restore it. Their `presentation-mode-test.sh` checks that `bar-off` is set after `presentation on`, so on a tree with both changes it fails at `presentation on hides the bar`.
- **#11803** changes the `omarchy:summary` of `bin/omarchy-toggle-bar` to "(on hides the bar, off shows it)". That summary is shown in the command help.

**Impact:** whichever of these merges alongside this fix would hide the bar when it should show it and show it when it should hide it (or, for #11803, document the reverse of the actual behaviour). The combination raises no merge conflict, and presentation mode itself reports no error; only the presentation PRs' own shell test catches it.

**Suggested change:** in whichever PR lands second, swap the two `omarchy-toggle-bar` calls in `bin/omarchy-toggle-presentation`; the presentation test already expects the right outcome and passes unchanged once the calls are swapped. Drop or reword #11803's summary if this fix merges.

**Note:** #7023, #12150, #12155 and #13451 also implement the on/off inversion in the same files, and each conflicts with this PR in a local merge, so only one of them can land as is. #7023 does not update `omarchy-toggle-fullscreen-desktop`; in an isolated run with #7023's wrapper on the current `quattro` tip, entering full screen showed the bar instead of hiding it, and the toggle no longer left full screen. This PR includes that caller.

**Optional:** unknown arguments (for example `show`, `hide`, `ON`) still pass through to `omarchy-toggle`, which prints `Usage: omarchy-toggle <flag-name> [toggle|on|off]`, while `omarchy-toggle-bar` exits 0. This is the same on the base. After this PR, that usage line describes `on`/`off` in the flag's sense, the opposite of the bar command's. A usage arm in the `case` of `omarchy-toggle-bar` would give a correct message and a non-zero exit.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Head `3110117e`, base `quattro` at `2fbac0c8`; the four changed files are identical on the current `quattro` tip. `omarchy-toggle-bar` (11 argument forms × 2 start states) and `omarchy-toggle-fullscreen-desktop` (24 cases) were run on the base, the head and a local merge onto the current `quattro` tip, and the `omarchy` dispatcher route on the base and the head, in an isolated sandbox with synthetic home directories. `toggle-test.sh` was run, including cross runs (head test on base scripts and the reverse) and the mutants above. Related PRs were checked from their diffs and by local merges with this PR onto the `quattro` tip; the presentation tests of #12422 and #12730 were run on those merges. Not run: the graphical acceptance test, the full `test/shell` and `test/cli` suites, and the shell IPC nudge (`omarchy-shell -q omarchy.bar syncHidden`, unchanged by this PR). No live desktop or real bar was used.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
